one_line: Streamer dashboard with an AI teammate for proposing, teaching, and executing production setup workflows.
what_it_does: Provides shared streamer/agent controls for commands, alerts, promotions, overlays, and clip editing, with proposal review and human approval before consequential changes.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates against the same production state as the streamer and uses a proposal-review-approval flow rather than unreliable screen scraping; this is materially more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes first-class agent seat, shared state, and shared audit trail.
Proposal → Review → Approval → Execution workflow is explicitly described.
execution_rationale: The contact sheets show a substantial dark streamer dashboard across multiple states and the packet describes several coherent workflows; the exact end-to-end completion is not fully legible in the small sheets.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion frame sheets show repeated dashboard, configuration, and workflow states.
Description identifies concrete surfaces including chat, alerts, overlays, clip studio, and approval cards.
impact_rationale: Streamers are a clear audience with repetitive, costly production work, and the product addresses that work while retaining human control over risky changes.
impact_evidence: Description identifies one-person production studios and many recurring production tasks.
Agent-assisted setup and clip workflows directly target time and complexity.
creativity_rationale: The built-in AI teammate and proposal-first collaboration model are a strong, memorable synthesis for streaming operations.
creativity_evidence: Human-controlled themed proposals rather than unrestricted agent execution.
Guided tours and shared workspace extend the concept beyond a chatbot add-on.
usability_note: Approval cards and guided tours suggest good control, though the dense dashboard may be demanding for new users.
advance_reason: Strong agent-centered workflow and credible value for a defined audience.

one_line: A risk, authorization, and discovery layer for safer WebMCP tool registration.
what_it_does: Scans WebMCP apps, classifies consequential tools, requires authorization and verification metadata, and publishes machine-readable semantics for agents.
leverage_rationale: The product addresses a capability gap specific to structured agent surfaces: enforceable risk semantics, confirmation requirements, completion verification, and discovery that generic UI automation cannot provide reliably.
leverage_evidence: Census claims 75 tools and 49 mutating tools with no enforceable risk metadata.
Description specifies refusal to register consequential tools lacking authorization, confirmation metadata, or completion verifiers.
/.well-known/agent.json publishes machine-readable tool semantics.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a focused library and a concrete audit/census workflow; frame sheets show technical dashboard and result states, though small text limits verification of the full flow.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show repeated application, processing, and highlighted review/result states.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
Concrete API and policy behavior are described.
impact_rationale: Every WebMCP app exposing mutating tools has a safety and discovery problem, and this directly targets authorization, user confirmation, and reliable agent operation.
impact_evidence: Measured problem across 75 tools and five applications.
Consequential actions such as checkout, delete, and submit are explicitly addressed.
creativity_rationale: Turning informal tool descriptions into enforceable, discoverable risk contracts is an original and important infrastructure direction.
creativity_evidence: Combines registration enforcement, completion verification, and agent discovery.
Treats risk metadata as testable CI/runtime semantics rather than prose.
usability_note: The infrastructure is conceptually clear, but adoption requires integrating registration and policy metadata into app development workflows.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly WebMCP-specific infrastructure with credible evidence and strong differentiation.

one_line: A Live Canvas where agents compose bounded, personalized interfaces inside ordinary web pages.
what_it_does: Lets an agent curate storefront results, generate dashboards, and create bespoke reports within constrained UI regions using approved components.
leverage_rationale: The core product is agent composition of live UI and shared state, not merely data retrieval; bounded canvas composition is difficult to reproduce comparably through generic browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Description defines a WebMCP Live Canvas region that the agent can redesign.
Storefront, dashboard, and distribution demos all use agent-generated interface composition.
Approved card presets constrain untrusted content while preserving live interaction.
execution_rationale: The sheets show a coherent progression from storefront/source content to composed product/result pages, but the tiny contact sheets do not prove every described demo end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show source content, changing storefront states, dialogs, and populated result pages.
Description covers three distinct demos with concrete bounded interaction models.
impact_rationale: The approach could help shoppers research and help teams create dashboards or reports without bespoke frontend work; each audience has a concrete personalization need.
impact_evidence: Storefront scenario addresses research and cart abandonment.
Dashboard and datatable scenarios target personalized analytics and reporting.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-interface is a genuinely novel interaction model, especially the constrained agent-authored canvas that remains safe and composable.
creativity_evidence: Explicit BYOUI thesis.
Three scales of composition: curated results, blank dashboards, and distributable components.
usability_note: Bounded presets and generated layouts support safety, but agent-authored interfaces could still be unpredictable to users.
advance_reason: Exceptional originality with strong WebMCP centrality and credible visible product motion.

one_line: A browser extension that records repeatable browser tasks and exposes them as reusable WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Allows no-code recording or JSON import of parameterized workflows, then executes them on arbitrary websites with history and logs when an agent invokes the resulting tool.
leverage_rationale: Recorded workflows replace repeated agent interpretation of arbitrary UIs with deterministic, parameterized tool execution; WebMCP makes user-created processes discoverable in-page.
leverage_evidence: Description says users create processes once and reuse them instead of having an agent rediscover the UI.
Processes expose parameters and execution history as WebMCP tools.
Works on sites without native WebMCP or APIs.
execution_rationale: The video sheets show repeated app states, workflow diagrams, and execution/status panels consistent with a working process builder, while the public repo and detailed implementation description reinforce completeness.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show workflow/configuration states and changing execution output.
Description identifies no-code recording, JSON import, parameters, execution history, and third-party site handling.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals have many repetitive browser workflows, and reusable processes can reduce time, token use, and operational inconsistency.
impact_evidence: Concrete examples include creating leads, customers, todos, articles, and CRM updates.
Sharing and debugging use cases are explicitly described.
creativity_rationale: User-authored WebMCP tools layered over arbitrary existing websites is a strong and ambitious extension of browser automation.
creativity_evidence: No-code recording turns personal browser behavior into agent capabilities.
Combines prior process-guidance technology with browser-native WebMCP.
usability_note: No-code recording and parameter support are promising, though third-party page variability remains a practical friction point.
red_flags: Packet notes current ChatGPT discovery requires custom instructions.
standouts: Personalized tool creation without changing target sites
advance_reason: High practical value and a strong, differentiated WebMCP use case despite discovery limitations.

one_line: A read-only, evidence-aware architecture graph shared by people and agents.
what_it_does: Maps project entities and relationships, traces architecture paths, surfaces bypasses and security findings, and preserves uncertainty through structured WebMCP queries.
leverage_rationale: Exact entity IDs, bounded structured queries, shared visual focus, and fail-closed uncertainty handling give agents reliable architecture access beyond filenames, screenshots, or generic UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Five WebMCP tools operate on the same graph and selection state as the human UI.
Unknown or fuzzy requests fail closed without changing selection.
Tools are read-only and return bounded, evidence-aware results.
execution_rationale: The sheets show a substantial graph/explorer interface with changing diagram and lower status panels; the detailed packet describes a disciplined graph core and explicit safety boundaries.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show workflow/architecture canvas states and execution/status regions.
Description specifies deterministic IDs, provenance, validation, SHA-256 integrity, analyzers, and uncertainty states.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Large software teams and AI-assisted engineering both need current architecture and security visibility; exposing bypasses and unknowns has credible value.
impact_evidence: Target problem is drift among screens, routes, permissions, services, data, and audit rules.
The demo explicitly exposes a direct UI-to-handler bypass.
creativity_rationale: The combination of semantic architecture graph, evidence provenance, explicit uncertainty, and shared human-agent exploration is notably original.
creativity_evidence: Unknown, Blind Spot, Needs Proof, and Review are first-class states.
Read-only insight without production mutation authority is a deliberate interaction model.
usability_note: A dense architecture graph can be difficult to navigate, but shared focus and bounded tools mitigate that complexity.
advance_reason: Strong engineering depth and meaningful agent-specific architecture workflow.

one_line: An agent plans trips by geocoding real places, drawing routes, and pinning the itinerary live on a map.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP to let an agent invoke live Mapbox map capabilities for place search, markers, directions, framing, and itinerary/activity updates.
leverage_rationale: The agent directly controls a live map and shares its rendered state with the user; structured geospatial actions are more precise and observable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent geocodes places, pulls walking routes, drops pins, draws the route, and frames the map live.
Map capabilities close over the live map instance and register through document.modelContext.
Itinerary and activity log rebuild from actual calls.
execution_rationale: The packet provides unusually clear end-to-end scope and the motion sheets visibly show a map workspace with agent panel/status states; the live demo is reported alive.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show repeated map views with an expanded agent/activity panel.
Description specifies end-to-end trip planning and visible activity logging.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Travelers have a clear planning need, and a live itinerary with real places and walking routes directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Concrete Paris half-day trip scenario with Eiffel Tower, cafe, Louvre, and walking directions.
Real geocoding and routing are part of the demonstrated workflow.
creativity_rationale: The live map as an agent-controlled rendering surface is a strong, coherent interaction model beyond a text-only trip answer.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly rejects static-image or text-only map demos.
Combines data-layer tools with a live visual rendering surface.
usability_note: Live visual feedback and activity logging make the workflow understandable; requiring an Anthropic API key adds setup friction.
advance_reason: Very strong execution evidence and a convincing live-state WebMCP demonstration.

one_line: A GitHub-like review workspace where agents inspect code, propose issues, and act only after human approval.
what_it_does: Shares repository context, inline findings, editable proposals, approval state, activity trace, and dynamically changing WebMCP tools between human and agent.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic tool exposure tied to exact transient workspace state and approval status is central; a remote API or generic UI agent would not reproduce the same safe, context-sensitive collaboration comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Tool surface changes from 7 to 9 to 10 tools based on workspace state.
Final creation accepts only the exact approved proposal and rejects stale, edited, dismissed, or unknown proposals.
Human and agent share annotations, proposal, approval, and activity state.
execution_rationale: The video evidence shows repeated repository/review UI states and highlighted findings, while the packet specifies a complete review-to-issue flow with explicit lifecycle handling and tests.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show structured repository pages, review states, and highlighted output regions.
Description details inspect, annotate, propose, approve, create, and visible activity feed.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Code review is a real, recurring team workflow, and the product addresses both review throughput and human control over issue creation.
impact_evidence: Concrete workflow identifies serious substantiated problem and prepares an editable issue.
Approval boundary prevents unintended repository mutation.
creativity_rationale: State-dependent WebMCP capability negotiation combined with exact approval references is an unusually strong human-agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Capabilities reconcile as workspace state changes.
Approval revocation on edits and exact-reference creation are carefully designed semantics.
usability_note: Inline findings, editable proposals, and visible activity make the collaboration legible; the controlled fixture scope limits real-world breadth.
red_flags: Uses local fixture data rather than a real GitHub backend/API.
advance_reason: One of the clearest demonstrations of WebMCP changing the collaboration model rather than merely wrapping an API.

one_line: An infinite visual research board where people add raw material and agents organize, connect, and arrange it.
what_it_does: Combines rich board content, selection-aware structured context, multimodal canvas images, semantic clustering, and agent actions for cards, links, layouts, and annotations.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes the board’s structured state, human selection as an attention signal, visual canvases, and permitted semantic actions while leaving geometry and safety to the browser; generic UI automation cannot match this precision on a large mixed-media board.
leverage_evidence: Selected items are returned first and drawings/canvases can be supplied as images.
Agents provide meaning and requested arrangements while the browser handles positions, collisions, and layout.
Same internal tool definitions serve human and agent actions.
execution_rationale: The sheets show repeated dark board/workflow states and output previews, while the packet describes a broad but coherent implementation with local persistence, layout algorithms, and multimodal handling.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show repeated board/task states and generated preview/result surfaces.
Description identifies IndexedDB, synchronization, embeddings, clustering, spatial indexing, media/document parsing, and drawing support.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Researchers, students, creatives, and knowledge workers have a real need to capture ideas without premature structure and later make sense of large mixed-media collections.
impact_evidence: Supports notes, links, files, drawings, documents, media, and spreadsheets on one board.
Selection-aware context and automatic clustering directly address overload and organization friction.
creativity_rationale: The hybrid structured/visual board and the rule that agents request semantic arrangement without controlling coordinates are deeply original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Inspired by the historical Mundaneum but reimagined for multimodal human-agent collaboration.
Combines visual canvas rasterization, semantic embeddings, layout algorithms, and safe agent actions.
usability_note: The no-folder capture model is inviting, but the breadth of media and spatial organization creates a substantial learning curve.
standouts: Selection as explicit agent attention signal
Semantic intent separated from browser-controlled geometry
advance_reason: Highly ambitious and distinctive product with unusually deep WebMCP/state integration.

one_line: A shared visual desk for organizing decisions, options, tradeoffs, unresolved considerations, and evidence with an agent.
what_it_does: Lets users create decision spaces, add options and pros/cons, surface unresolved questions, link sources, and collaborate with an agent through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured decision entities and shared state give an agent a better surface than generic UI driving, but the core workflow remains achievable with a general agent plus ordinary form interaction.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists WebMCP operations for desks, decisions, options, tradeoffs, unresolved considerations, and external sources.
Frame sheets show repeated desk/table/dialog states and visible state changes.
Site tools popup is shown in the described product.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent decision workspace through creation and interaction states, and the packet provides a focused feature set; exact end-to-end agent completion is only partly legible.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show repeated product states, dialogs, and changed decision/table views.
Description identifies desk creation, option/tradeoff interaction, unresolved sticky notes, source linking, and tool discovery.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: People regularly struggle with complex personal, academic, and purchase decisions, and externalizing tradeoffs can provide credible cognitive value.
impact_evidence: Concrete class-registration dilemma motivates the product.
Description names classes, laptops, and daily choices as use cases.
creativity_rationale: A visual decision desk with unresolved considerations and agent collaboration is a fresh synthesis, though decision-mapping is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Blue unresolved-consideration sticky notes make uncertainty visible.
Shared thinking space combines structured tradeoffs with linked source material.
usability_note: The visual desk and explicit unresolved items should make deliberation easier than keeping tradeoffs in memory.
advance_reason: Credible and useful productivity concept with solid execution evidence, though WebMCP delta is less transformative than the leading projects.

one_line: A mail client that gives an agent structured inbox, thread, contact, and personal writing-style tools while keeping sending human-approved.
what_it_does: Lets an agent find threads, reload context, draft replies in the user’s voice, and place them in an editable compose window; sending requires explicit approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured thread search, contact resolution, context loading, and style retrieval address the hidden state and tone problems that make DOM-driven email agents unreliable; the human approval boundary is central.
leverage_evidence: Named tools include search_emails, resolve_contact, read_thread, get_writing_style, and send_email.
Draft lands visibly in an editable compose window and send requires explicit UI approval.
Tool calls are logged live in the sidebar.
execution_rationale: The sheets show repeated mail-client states, technical/task panels, and highlighted or changed content; the packet describes a complete daily flow, though small text limits direct verification of exact drafts.
execution_evidence: Three motion sheets show inbox/composition-like interfaces across multiple workflow states.
Description specifies finding, context reload, style-based drafting, approval, and logging.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Email is a widespread, repetitive knowledge-work burden, and reducing search, rereading, and drafting time while preserving approval has clear practical value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies daily email as an hour-or-two burden for working users.
Reply-to-thread workflow directly targets repetitive work and personal tone.
creativity_rationale: A deliberately AI-free mail client that teaches the external agent the user’s voice, while keeping the compose/send boundary visible, is a strong interaction design.
creativity_evidence: No AI inside the client; WebMCP is the agent teaching surface.
Personal writing style is exposed as structured context rather than generic generation.
usability_note: One-sentence requests and editable drafts simplify email, while explicit send approval supports trust.
red_flags: Voice/style quality cannot be assessed from silent contact sheets and no transcript.
standouts: Structured retrieval plus personal style context
advance_reason: Clear high-value workflow with meaningful WebMCP leverage and strong safety/usability choices.
